answer.answer: The PVE34 10M run remains valid historical capacity evidence: it proved clean D1 progress on Nyx and identified DB/write coordination as the bottleneck. Later final-target testing superseded the fixed-worker tuning model with scenario-based autonomy governed by durable DB/Redis truth, explicit transient-fault behavior, and crash-safe recovery. Stage 3 D1 validation is still incomplete, so the next safe experiment is a bounded full D1 replay with Cortex, full dev-S3 verification, and TERM/KILL recovery proof.

claims.value: The PVE34 10M crossing run `split-lanes-64f-pve34-pvp2-other1-200k-to10m-20260523T115711Z` inserted `210624` rows, finished at `10.019M`, and crossed `10,000,000` at elapsed `442s` with `0` parser errors, retries, duplicates, or terminal markers. Its steady average from elapsed `220-490s` was about `403/sec`, late pre-stop average about `408/sec`, and drain average about `372/sec`. Summary recompute for `1-10019225`, sampled membership, S3, and final-chunk coverage checks passed; protected D2 Redis counts were unchanged, and PVE raw-player totals exactly matched `summary_activity` and `summary_time`. This established PVE34 as the best practical Nyx profile in that data band while showing that the write path, not fetch, was limiting throughput.

Later final-target evidence superseded PVE34 as an operating prescription, while preserving it as historical evidence. D1 passed alpha through eta plus theta across live-edge/catch-up, sustained speed, fixed `750ms` latency, random `200-1700ms` latency, gap/retry behavior, fake Bungie maintenance, connection-refused failures, and S3-first replay. D1 peaks were alpha `1425.1/s`, beta `1380.1/s`, gamma `1242.9/s`, delta `1016.9/s`, epsilon `1455.1/s`, and theta `2704.7/s`. Delta and epsilon recorded stop-edge work without turning it into a cursor, epsilon held it behind durable Redis truth, zeta and eta committed no PGCRs and created no permanent failed rows, and theta passed with clean DB/Redis/process checks plus fresh dev-S3 verification of `43` bundles / `43000` PGCRs. The resulting operating model is autonomous scenario handling and durable-state recovery, not a fixed PVE34 worker count.

claims.value: The non-negotiable model is: no durable skipped PGCRs; incomplete coverage must hold rollup behind durable Redis truth; stop-edge work must be recorded rather than promoted to a cursor; transient maintenance or connection failures must commit no PGCRs, create no permanent failed rows, and record transient stop reasons; fresh parser-owned S3 bundles require manifest/payload hash validation against ledger/source truth with zero mismatches/errors; production side effects remain off during validation; and recovery must survive TERM/KILL by resuming from durable DB/Redis truth without manual row repair. Small pending edge work at an artificial stop is acceptable only when durable state is safe and restart recovers truth. Final validation cannot be declared until validation processes are gone and DB/Redis cursors, dev-S3 prefixes, and remaining gaps by exact ID and reason are recorded.

claims.value: The next safe experiment is the still-unrun bounded Stage 3 D1 sequence, not another blind worker-count increase: first prove the final branch, HEAD, status/diff, exact Linux binary SHA256s, schema, environment, and validation-safe side effects; set `WARMIND_D1_NEXUS_PGCR_CACHE_DIR`; then run an agreed full D1 slice with D1 Cortex while checking raw/cache/failed invariants, ModeZero semantics, and summary/carry/WAU/DAU jobs as applicable. Verify fresh dev-S3 bundles against D1 DB or ledger truth with zero mismatches/errors and record verifier rate, then perform oracle plus TERM/KILL restart tests requiring durable resume and no manual row repair. The earlier basic90 verifier covered only `10` bundles, so it does not complete the full intended-coverage gate.

answer.answer: Revised plan: replace the single mega-base with capacity-isolated modular sites. Keep every level-0 Core below 1,000 capacity, use only verified Update 1 equipment, and validate logistics and defense behavior in-game before scaling. Durable checkpoint saved as checkpoint:fc575c35-645e-f81e-ccdd-d8b0679ab747.

claims.value: Superseding proposal: use a distributed architecture consisting of a protected starter hub plus satellite extraction and processing cells, each independently kept below its level-0 Core’s 1,000 capacity. Keep the starter hub to low-heat essentials and reserved defense headroom. Do not colocate a 500-capacity Constructorizer and 650-capacity Facturer because together they exceed the entire level-0 budget and disable Fire Wave protection. Use only Update 1 equipment; exclude the site-flagged hidden Chimeran Power Generator and treat level 10–15 Forgotten Engine items as out of scope.

Proposed live logistics: give every production cell dedicated point-to-point input and output transport, with separate input and output storage so starvation and blockage remain visible; use only transport tiers confirmed as currently unlocked in Update 1. A full output buffer must isolate or stop its cell rather than back up unrelated production. Numeric thresholds are pending measurement: exports stop when local stock reaches the measured low mark and resume only after it recovers to the high mark. Ore Excavator v.1 supplies 60/120/240 items/min on Impure/Normal/Pure nodes; exact downstream sizing and logistics throughput must be verified in-game.

Proposed exports are surplus Basic Building Material, smelted Titanium/Wolfram/Calcium blocks, Basic Electronics, and Ceramics, but only after retaining local Core-upgrade, construction, and defense reserves. Reserve explicit capacity headroom for one currently unlocked defensive structure or ammo-production loop before adding production; its identity, heat cost, and Fire Wave effectiveness remain unverified. Basic Item Printers can make building materials and ammo inside Habitats, while exceeding Core capacity disables Fire Wave protection.

Test next: (1) whether disconnected, unpowered, paused, or idle machines count toward Core capacity and what site boundary controls accounting; (2) whether Base Core Amplifier v.1/v.2 actually add +50/+20 capacity or follow the conflicting temperature fields of −250/−20; (3) which Update 1 transport tiers are unlocked and their measured throughput, merge priority, overflow, blockage, and restart behavior; (4) container capacities and real consumption rates needed for numeric low/high buffer marks; (5) exact recipes and sustained rates for Basic Building Material, smelted blocks, Basic Electronics, and Ceramics exports; and (6) which defense or ammo loop is unlocked, its heat cost, and its effectiveness during a Fire Wave.

decisions: Adopt distributed capacity-isolated production sites instead of one mega-base.
Reserve defense capacity before expanding production.
Exclude hidden Chimeran power and level 10–15 Forgotten Engine content.
Use buffered cells whose exports stop at a measured low mark and resume at a measured high mark.

Unlocked logistics tiers and operational behavior.
Storage capacities and suitable buffer thresholds.
Verified export recipes and sustained rates.
Available defense provision, heat cost, and Fire Wave performance.
next_actions: Run a controlled Core-accounting and 1,000-capacity protection test.
Benchmark available transport tiers, including blockage and recovery.
Measure storage capacity and consumption before setting thresholds.
Select, budget, and Fire-Wave-test one defense or ammo loop.
